claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 specimens possess an intrinsic hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical structure contains spatially distributed potential crack-nucleation sites.
Early-stage acoustic-emission signals are reliable precursors to yielding and fracture events in HfNbTiVAl10.
Localized deformation patterns measured by DIC are reliable precursors to yielding and fracture events in HfNbTiVAl10.
High-speed imaging can calibrate the relationship between AE/DIC signatures and microcrack initiation and evolution.
AE frequency, amplitude, and event rate indicate the onset and growth of microcracks in the hierarchical structure.
Spatially resolved DIC strain localization indicates the onset and growth of microcracks in the hierarchical structure.
Early AE signals and localized DIC strain concentrations act as precursors to microcrack formation.
After high-speed-imaging calibration, AE/DIC signals can be quantitatively linked to yielding thresholds.
After high-speed-imaging calibration, AE/DIC signals can be quantitatively linked to fracture thresholds.
The integrated AE/DIC model can rapidly estimate Young's modulus.
The integrated AE/DIC model can rapidly estimate yield strength.
The integrated AE/DIC model can predict fracture initiation and broader fracture-related behavior.
The framework will improve decision-making speed by approximately 30% relative to full-scale finite-element simulations.
The framework will improve predictive accuracy by 5–10% relative to full-scale finite-element simulations.
Excessive or insufficiently distinct AE noise caused by the complex microstructure may invalidate the predictive relationship.
Failure of DIC to resolve critical strain localization may cause the hypothesis to fail.
Inadequate imaging calibration of microcrack evolution may cause the predictive model to fail.
Extreme strain rates or microstructural inconsistencies may invalidate the learned predictive correlations.
Analogous studies of heterogeneous microstructures suggest that AE and DIC can track imminent failure events.
